definitions: To unintentionally help or benefit someone or something, often an opponent or a negative situation.
To contribute to or become part of a particular situation or outcome, often one that is undesirable.
examples: His comments might play into the hands of the opposition.
Don't let their arguments play into your insecurities.
The recent events play into the narrative of economic decline.
pastTenses: played into (simple past), played into (present perfect), played into (past perfect)
